p.t: The Cruise: Fun-Loving Brits at Sea
p.d: It's the final day of the cruise for the travellers, but before heading home they explore the holiday hot-spot for the rich and famous - the Greek party capital of Mykonos

p.t: The Cruise: Fun-Loving Brits at Sea
p.d: The Mediterranean holiday-makers enjoy a trip to the Greek capital Athens, including a visit to the ruins of Hadrian's Library, botanical gardens and a flea market

Susan embarks on a cruise in Australia, beginning in Melbourne. First she hops on one of the city's iconic trams to take in the sights. Susan then sails west overnight to Portland to view the coastal vistas of the Great Ocean Road and the Twelve Apostles, described as the world's largest war memorial. On Kangaroo Island and at Hanson Bay Wildlife Sanctuary, Susan spots her first kangaroo in the wild, and later spies a koala. In Adelaide, she takes a wine-tasting excursion to the McLaren Vale. The final stop is Tasmania, where Susan discovers dark truths of Britain's colonial past at Port Arthur

p.t: Warship: Life in the Royal Navy
p.d: JJ Chalmers takes on the endurance course at the Commando Training Centre, which he passed with flashing colours when he first began his career. He also discovers what the future of naval warfare might look like, from intense training to hi-tech weapons. As Julia Bradbury's time on the mighty HMS Prince of Wales comes to an end, she helps the ship's crew as they prepare to enter a foreign port

p.t: Warship: Life in the Royal Navy
p.d: Kate Humble and JJ Chalmers are given unprecedented access to the Royal Navy. Cameras on board a British warship follow the hunt for a Russian submarine. Kate gets special clearance to go behind the scenes at Britain's secretive submarine base at Faslane in Scotland. JJ reveals what it takes to be an elite Royal Marine Commando as he journeys back to the beginning of his military career

How the invention of the railway at the dawn of the 19th century changed the world, and the lives of engineers such as Stephenson, Telford and Brunel. Though great wealth was made on the back of steam power, many rail lines couldn't break even and huge swathes of them were eventually axed from existence. Cameras also reveal how Britain's railways are on the move again as HS2 plans to connect the most influential cities with their own high-speed, high-capacity rail line

The story of how this country was built from the ground up - by filling in a map of Britain's transport networks through the ages, and focusing on the UK's love-hate relationship with motorways. Since their fitful start in the 1950s, through the glamour of the swinging 60s, and the backlash against urban planning gone mad, we chart the progress of these epic engineering projects as they came to dominate our landscape

Michael explores the country, a huge and once oil-rich nation that has been called the most dangerous in South America, which contrasts with its beautiful scenery. He talks to investigative reporter Ana Vanessa Herrero about the shock re-election of Nicolás Maduro as president and the country's slide into totalitarian rule
National and international news

Paul Merton narrates a compilation of clips from disastrous motorhome holidays, including a campervan invaded by giant spiders, a tyre blowing out at high speed on a motorway, and holidaymakers in the Lake District getting into trouble as they drive up Hardknott Pass

Sue Radford finally has the chance to focus on herself and embarks on a dramatic weight-loss transformation that gives her a confidence she has never had before, but an online backlash and endless speculation about how she lost the weight threaten to overshadow her achievement. Meanwhile, eldest daughter Sophie is determined to take back control of her life and stop herself slipping into a downward spiral, so commits to a gruelling endurance challenge that will push her to her physical and emotional limits

Dallas Cowboys v Washington Commanders (Kick-off 9.25pm). Dermot O'Leary, Sam Quek, and Osi Umenyiora present coverage of the week two NFC East match at AT&T Stadium in Arlington. The Cowboys defeated the Commanders home and away last season, but like Washington, they failed to find the consistent form required to get close to the play-off places, so both teams will be hoping for improved campaigns this time around

Houston Texans v Cincinnati Bengals (Kick-off 6.00pm). All the action from the AFC match at NRG Stadium. The teams have not met since 2023, when the Texans claimed a narrow 23-20 away win at Paycor Stadium. Houston reached the divisional play-offs last term, where they were eliminated by New England Patriots, while the Bengals failed to reach the post-season

A stolen motorcycle leads deputies up a mountain, deputies chase a stolen car driven by a 13-year-old, and Kern County's Air Support Unit observes a fleeing suspect ditch his minibike

Late evening on a quiet, leafy street in Dudley, gunfire rips through a young woman's front door, with one shot striking her in the hip. West Midland police's major crime team takes charge, tasked to find out who could have committed such a crime, and a manhunt begins when CCTV footage shows a vehicle speeding away. From there, the investigation intensifies and a small but significant mistake by the getaway driver means the vehicle can be tracked
A badly injured tortoise needs an innovative procedure and the wardens investigate an eagle's death. As night falls, a car crash turns into a manhunt

Dr Jeff treats a cherished bloodhound puppy that refuses to eat. Dr Petra comes to the rescue of a cat that has swallowed a handful of hair ties
The family of Mutt, a Villabos employee who recently passed away, meet the dog he chose for them. Plus, Tia and M2 go on a wild goose chase near a middle school.
Tiana is shocked by the condition of a stray dog after a challenging rescue. Tia and the family tackle their messy pigeon problem

Jackson Galaxy helps a soft-spoken musician who feels abused by her cat and is ashamed she cannot figure out how to prevent her pet's behaviour
Pete Nelson constructs a thrill-seeker's dream treetop escape in Washington, complete with a bouncy-bridge entryway and a zip-line through the forest
One dog loves ice-cream, while another keeps getting his head stuck in things. Plus, a parrot with a habit of rapping and swearing
A game of underwater copycat shows how smart dolphins really are. Plus, how hyenas can eat pretty much anything and geckos' ability to apparently defy gravity
A squirrel's ability to hide up to 10,000 nuts in one season - and still find them again. Plus, alligators' fondness for music and whether a bug can survive in space
Shaun braves wet conditions in Covington to bring down a friendly stray that obviously misses his home
Shaun travels to La Conner to rescue Play-Play, whose distraught owner watches nearly 70 feet below, while Tom is called out on a late-night mission
An interview with Billy, the Brown family patriarch who - along with his wife Amy - chose to raise his seven children in the Alaskan wilderness
Businessman Brad Jennings wants to complete his new office with three tanks, so the team work on three complementary interiors which include a working fireplace

p.t: Crossing England in a Punt: River of Dreams
p.d: Tom Fort embarks on a 170-mile journey down the River Trent in his own custom-built punt. The presenter encounters the power stations that generate much of the nation's electricity, meets veterans of the floods of 1947 and learns about a Bronze Age boatman who made a life on the banks as he discovers the waterway's 3,000-year history

Water has always been the driving force in East Anglia - its ebb and flow has shaped the fenland. The ancient wetlands once covered hundreds of square miles, but today, well over 90 per cent has been drained and converted into farmland. Every winter, thousands of whooper swans return to the flooded pastures of the Ouse washes from their Arctic breeding grounds. On the Welney Wetlands, spring sees 'mad' march hares boxing over mates. It was once thought these bouts were male hares boxing for dominance, but it is often the females throwing the punches to fend off the attentions of over-eager suitors. Narrated by Toby Jones

p.t: The Riviera: A History in Pictures
p.d: Part one of two. Actor Richard E Grant follows in the footsteps of artists who lived and painted on France's Cote d'Azur, renowned for its sunny climate. The first edition focuses on the relationship between modern art and the location's development as an international tourist haven. Cezanne, Monet and Renoir were captivated by the light and colour of the landscape in the 19th century and their resultant work advertised the region's beauty. Meanwhile, the area's vivid hues inspired Henri Matisse to adopt a new palette that set modern art on the route to abstraction

The playwright shares the story of how the black comedy was born, from the first bizarre germ of idea that got him started, through to the casting, and the challenges that came with his decision to make the leader of Sinn Fein so central to his narrative. David's recollections also include details of his approach to writing, his feelings on the filming of theatrical productions generally, and his thoughts on the importance of catharsis and comedy when it comes to modern plays

Belfast loyalist Eric Miller experiences a psychotic episode and mistakes his five-week-old granddaughter for Gerry Adams. Generations of sectarian trauma convince him that his cultural heritage is under siege and he must act. Stephen Rea stars in Vicky Featherstone's 2019 adaptation of David Ireland's black comedy, which mixes performance footage from the stage of London's Royal Court with location shooting in Belfast

The discovery of an ancient music score deep within the storerooms of the Louvre leads musical historians on a mission to realise its potential, sung through a modern arrangement. But to hear the piece as the Greeks did 2,400 years ago, it has to be played on period instruments. This documentary follows the journey from the Greek cities of Anatolia to the Ptolemies' Egypt, from the mythical site of Delphi to discoveries made in Pompeii, where archaeological excavations have unearthed instrument remains

Archaeologist and historian Richard Miles explores the roots of civilisation in a series that runs from the creation of the first cities in Mesopotamia some 6,000 years ago, to the decline and fall of the Roman Empire. He travels to Syria, Egypt, Anatolia and southern Greece to examine how the first societies were created and organised, with agriculture, city-building, religion, art and trade the basic pillars from which these complex social systems emerged

p.d: Time-travelling teenager Marty McFly is transported back to the days of the Wild West, where he strives to save his eccentric scientist friend Doc Brown from death at the hands of a villainous gunslinger. Final instalment in the sci-fi comedy trilogy, starring Michael J Fox, Christopher Lloyd, Mary Steenburgen and Thomas F Wilson

Documentary about four rival families - leopards, hyenas, wild dogs and lions - trying to claim a rich corner of Zambia as their home. Leopard mother Olimba's world is turned upside down by the arrival of wild dog Storm and her chaotic pack. But just when the dogs are beginning to settle into the kingdom and welcome a litter of puppies, an even more powerful force appears on the horizon - lions. Narrated by David Attenborough

Live coverage of the men's individual time-trial in the annual event, which comes from Montréal. Remco Evenepoel of Belgium has won this title in each of the previous three years, beating Australia's Jay Vine into second place in Rwanda 12 months ago, with Evenepoel's compatriot Ilan Van Wilder taking bronze

An FBI agent is recruited to join an elite government task force based on the border between the US and Mexico, charged with preventing drugs being smuggled into the country. The team is sent on a secret mission, and the new recruit is forced to question everything she believes in order to survive. Crime drama, starring Emily Blunt, Josh Brolin and Benicio Del Toro

The drug war on the US-Mexico border has escalated as the cartels have begun trafficking terrorists across the US border. Federal agent Matt Graver re-teams with operative Alejandro Gillick to fight the enemy forces. Thriller sequel, starring Josh Brolin, Benicio Del Toro and Isabela Merced

A 'skinny Jab' aims to reduce the appetite and slow down the emptying of the stomach contents. Reporter Pria Rai investigates the black market in cut-price 'skinny jabs' now being sold across the UK. She reveals what's really in these drugs and whether they are safe to use. She meets a young student who accidentally took an overdose of the drug, makes contact with one of the most prolific online sellers, goes undercover to reveal a new market for the drug hidden in plain sight and sends samples for testing. When those tests are returned, they reveal shocking results

The story of pioneering internet sensation Caroline Calloway. This young American girl's infamous viral scandals captivated audiences across the globe, with some of her followers left feeling duped and scammed

Mo McIntyre's grand plan to dig up an ancient stash of paramilitary weaponry and trade the arms for drugs gets under way. However, he is unaware that he is already under surveillance and that MI5 are onto him. Tommy Foster's firearms exam is brought forward before he has time to fully prepare. In a bid to convince Grace to come back to the work, Stevie calls round to her house and finally reveals something intimate about his personal life

In the aftermath of the shooting, the recruits are determined the McIntyres will pay for what they have done. Stevie goes to arrest the MI5 operatives - but Joseph orders Jonty to let them go free. Tina demands that James tells Mo his dark secret, and Grace accepts that she might have to break her promise to Angela

p.t: Lorraine Pascale: How to Be a Better Cook
p.d: Neil Forster is an impatient cook who reaches for the takeaway menu rather than making food from scratch. Lorraine shows him recipes including asparagus and cream cheese puff pastry tarts, a quick way to do a roast chicken and a neat shortcut to prepare a summer fruits pudding

Culinary writer Nigel Slater and Countryfile presenter Adam Henson join forces to grow and cook Britain's favourite food from a working farm in the Cotswolds, taking their lead from the top 50 buys on UK shoppers' supermarket lists. The duo begin by looking at how the growth of convenience food has led to a decline in traditional cooking. Nigel makes lasagne, the UK's most popular ready meal, trying to match the price of the off-the-shelf version, while down on the farm, Adam challenges himself to grow durum wheat, which is used to make pasta. There's also a look at the journey taken by beef from field to fork, before Nigel rustles up a Sunday roast

Documentary providing an insight into the lives of chimpanzees in Uganda's Kyambura Gorge, a deep, forested ravine running through the African savannah. For 15 years, the gorge has been cut off from the rest of the jungle, leaving the animals stranded with limited sources of food. The programme follows the 20 remaining chimps as alpha male Brutus tries to retain control of the family in its daily struggle to survive

p.t: The Big Deal with Steph McGovern
p.d: In the grand finale, three aspiring art-dealer pairs compete for £50,000 of British art. Guided by Steph, Cordelia de Freitas and Matt Carey-Williams, they enter London's Frieze Week, selling alongside established gallerists. After one pair is eliminated, the finalists pitch a six-figure sculpture to industry insiders at Frieze Sculpture Park

Live coverage of the women's individual time-trial in the annual event, which comes from Montréal. Marlen Reusser of Switzerland won this title last year in Rwanda, with Dutch riders Anna van der Breggen and Demi Vollering finishing second and third respectively

David Barby and Michael Baggot analyse items brought in by members of the public in Saltaire, West Yorkshire, including a set of sandwich markers and a 400-year-old gold coin. Meanwhile, Paul Martin visits Temple Newsam, a 17th-century house near Leeds, to learn about efforts to restore it to its former glory
Soap stars from past road trips search for antiques, with Hayley Tamaddon, Will Mellor and Danny Dyer aided by Raj Bisram, Paul Laidlaw and Natasha Raskin Sharp

Action from day four of the DP World Tour tournament, which took place at Wentworth Club in Virginia Water, Surrey. Sweden's Alex Noren won this event for the second time last year thanks to a play-off victory over France's Adrien Saddier. That victory meant he joined the likes of Luke Donald, Bernhard Langer and Tony Jacklin in winning this tournament twice

p.t: Secrets of the Bayeux Tapestry: Inside the Museum
p.d: Across 70 metres of exquisitely embroidered scenes, the Bayeux Tapestry tells the story of one of the most seismic events in British history - the Norman Invasion of 1066. For the last 950 years, this crucial part of Britain's national story has remained on the other side of the Channel in Bayeux, Normandy, but now it's coming back to the UK. Michael Palin narrates as historians and experts unravel its secrets, following the painstaking efforts to bring this priceless work of art back to the UK, where experts believe it was made, for a once-in-a-millennium exhibition at the British Museum

Seven celebrities of differing faiths and beliefs experience an emotional journey on a pilgrimage in north Wales, a route linked by churches dedicated to Celtic early Christian saints. Eshaan Akbar, Amanda Lovett, Spencer Matthews, Christine McGuinness, Tom Rosenthal, Sonali Shah and Michaela Strachan begin their adventure at Flint Castle on the bank of the Dee Estuary

Simon return to travel through more of the most remote landscapes on Earth, beginning by exploring Papua New Guinea's tropical rainforest in search of the tenkile tree kangaroo, one of the world's rarest animals. Covering just a tiny fraction of the planet's land surface, tropical rainforests hold more than half of the world's plant and animal species, and few places rival New Guinea for sheer diversity. The island is home to vast wilderness areas that remain little known to science, a lost world with countless species still undiscovered

The presenter sets out to uncover the mysteries of King Tutankhamun. Along the way, he encounters the enigmatic 'Alien King' Akhenaten and his wife, Nefertiti. Sailing down the Nile, he investigates how the Ancient Egyptians transported enormous stone blocks for their architectural marvels, including the 700-ton Colossi of Memnon. His quest then leads him into the Valley of the Kings, where he discovers the resting places of Akhenaten and King Tut's successor, Horemheb - before finally coming face to face with the mummy of the Boy King himself

The Battle of Raphia, fought in 217 BC near modern Rafah, which was a pivotal clash between Ptolemaic Egypt and the Seleucid Empire during the Fourth Syrian War. The outcome was a decisive victory for Ptolemy IV Philopator's forces, which secured Coele-Syria for Ptolemaic Egypt

p.t: Ramsay's 24 Hours to Hell and Back
p.d: Gordon Ramsay visits Stone's Throw, a family-owned fine dining restaurant on the Housatonic River in Seymour, Connecticut, to help the stressed owners improve their business. He and his team have just 24 hours to redecorate the uninspiring interior, making it more welcoming with a fresh colour palette, and update the menu, working around the clock with the restaurant staff, who must learn how to prepare and serve the new dishes as a team. The customers are asked to return the next day and dine in the upgraded restaurant

p.t: Ramsay's 24 Hours to Hell and Back
p.d: Gordon visits Bayou on the Vine, a family-run Cajun restaurant in the redeveloped Jazz District of Kansas City, Missouri that is struggling with an uncertain future. He and his team have just 24 hours to re-imagine the premises with a jazz theme, giving it a more authentic colour scheme, and original decor that includes musical instruments and family photographs

p.t: Ramsay's 24 Hours to Hell and Back
p.d: Gordon Ramsay visits Boardwalk 11, a Los Angeles gastropub and karaoke bar, where the late-night singing entertainment has become more appealing than the dining experience. He and his team have just 24 hours to redecorate the restaurant in a hip 1970s retro style as a fun disco lounge. They also revamp the menu to offer more fresh, simple fare, working around the clock with Boardwalk 11's staff, who must learn how to prepare the new dishes. The patrons are asked to return the next day and after dining in the upgraded establishment appraise their experience

p.t: Ramsay's 24 Hours to Hell and Back
p.d: Gordon Ramsay visits M'Dears Bakery and Bistro, a struggling restaurant in Los Angeles that specialises in Southern cuisine with a Californian twist and freshly baked goods. He and his team have just 24 hours to redecorate the premises, changing the dated dining area into a cosy and tasteful soul food destination. They also introduce a revamped menu, working around the clock with the staff of M'Dears, who must learn how to prepare the new dishes efficiently. The customers are asked to return the next day, dine in the updated restaurant and critique their experience

Greg Davies dishes out points when they're deserved and withholds them when they're not as he tries to make sense of Nina Conti filling her face with citrus fruits, Isy Suttie locating her saliva on Alex's jacket and Richard Ayoade chucking a doll's head at a gargoyle

In this compilation episode, it's Series 11 Finals Week! The best bakers from both heats compete in a week featuring party food pandemonium, supersized Showstoppers, a global sensation and puddings fit for a queen. But who will be crowned the winner?

Animated comedy, with the voices of Jerry Seinfeld, Renee Zellweger and Chris Rock

Lisa resolves to pursue a career in astronomy, but unfortunately her decision coincides with Chief Wiggum's hare-brained new initiative to reduce crime in Springfield - by illuminating the whole town all night. With the guest voice of Eric Idle

Hamish Blake throws down the gauntlet as he challenges the eight remaining teams to stop his Lego car from running a clear course through their terrain by setting booby traps, complete with pyrotechnics, mist and dust. Before going on to write classic fantasy books The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings, orphaned author JRR Tolkien finds friendship, love and artistic inspiration among a group of fellow outcasts at school. Eventually his experiences during the First World War inspire him to create a world of hobbits and wizards. Biopic, starring Nicholas Hoult, Lily Collins, Pam Ferris, Craig Roberts, and Derek Jacobi

Racing car driver and engineer Carroll Shelby is lured out of retirement during the 1960s, in a period where the sport is dominated by Italian companies. Ford Motors are hoping to revive their flagging fortunes by launching a racing division and securing a high-profile win at the prestigious Le Mans 24-hour race. Shelby takes up the challenge of headlining the plan to build a revolutionary new race car, but courts conflict within the company by recruiting unpredictable, short-tempered British driver Ken Miles to take the wheel. Fact-based drama, starring Matt Damon, Christian Bale, Jon Bernthal and Caitriona Balfe

A man who's given up on life following the loss of his wife and wants to end it all. When a young family moves in nearby, he meets his match in quick-witted Marisol, leading to a friendship that will turn his world around. Comedy drama, starring Tom Hanks, Mariana Trevino and Rachel Keller

Father Gabriele Amorth, chief exorcist of the Vatican, investigates a rundown abbey in San Sebastian. The owner, Julia, claims her 12-year-old son Henry has been possessed by a demon. The 10 remaining contestants face three tasks designed to test their bread-making skills, beginning by creating 12 perfect rye bread rolls shaped in any way they like and using as much flour as they dare. For the technical challenge they have to prepare Italian ciabatta using Paul's recipe, before ending with show-stopping centrepiece loaves that will have to make an impact on the table as well as on the judges. Paul Hollywood and Mary Berry then decide which of the contenders will be the week's star baker - and which of them is going home. Mel Giedroyc and Sue Perkins present

Judges Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood assess the remaining contestants' dessert-making skills, beginning with a signature challenge of a sponge containing a gooey sauce filling or a saucy surprise at the bottom. The technical round involves creating a tiramisu cake, before the contenders have to prepare a baked Alaska for the showstopper. Plus, presenter Sue Perkins explores the origins of Paignton pudding, a heavyweight version of which caused a riot in the Devon town in 1859

After last week's baked Alaska scandal - which led to Iain hanging up his apron and has since also seen Diana leave the show - judges Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood assess the remaining contestants' pastry skills. They begin with a signature challenge of a sweet custard tart of their own invention, ranging from rhubarb and custard to tropical Manchester tart. The technical round involves recreating Paul's recipe for mini pear pies, followed by their showpiece bake - a towering collection of three-tiered pies in just four hours. Along the way, Mel Giedroyc investigates the history of an ancient wedding centrepiece known as Bride Pie

The remaining six bakers have passed the halfway point of the contest, and now face three European bakes - beginning with yeast-leavened cakes, a tricky cross between cake and bread. Mary Berry then sets them the challenge of rustling up a Swedish princess torte, but they have their work cut out completing all 24 stages of the recipe in little more than two hours. They finish by creating their own version of the dobos torte, a multi-layered cake from Hungary. However, they must go one step further and bake a two-tiered version with an emphasis on caramel. Which of the bakers will come to a sticky end?

Presenters Mel Giedroyc and Sue Perkins set the remaining contestants three tasks involving pastry, beginning by asking them to make signature savoury parcels. For the technical challenge, they must prepare a cake that hails from the Brittany region of France - the kouign amann, which none of the bakers has ever heard of - before creating two different types of eclair in the showstopper round. Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood judge the hopefuls' efforts before deciding who is star baker and who is going home

p.t: Evil Lives Here: Shadows of Death
p.d: The case of Frank Buschauer, convicted of drowning his wife, Cynthia Hrisco, in a whirlpool bathtub in February 2000. The arduous police investigation stretched on for years, though the family maintains the death was a terrible accident

p.t: Evil Lives Here: Shadows of Death
p.d: In 1980, a college freshman failed to return after a night out. Police followed her trail to a mysterious lake house, but 40 years later they still have no answers

p.t: Evil Lives Here: Shadows of Death
p.d: In Dallas, Texas, surgical patients were falling victim to a monster with a medical degree. Dr Christopher Duntsch - aka Dr Death - was later found guilty of gross malpractice

On the night of November 29, 2006, Avis Banks, a daycare worker, was found shot and stabbed to death in the garage of her Ridgeland, Mississippi home. Her body was discovered by her fiance Keyon Pittman, and it appeared as if the perpetrator had kicked in their back door
In 2006, Nick Castree's abusive father Ronald turned up unannounced at his door. Nick feared his father, but had no idea of the secret life he had been living
In 1995 Hermosa Beach, aspiring model Linda Sobek chases stardom, but a shoot with a photographer hiding dark secrets ends in tragedy
After a killer strikes a Louisiana farmer, police examine a pilfering maid, a withdrawn farmhand and a duplicitous wife, all with a motive for murder
Alina Burroughs travels to Michigan, where Linda Stermer stands accused of killing her husband, Todd, by setting a fire. Alina takes a close look at the charred clues

Ben Shephard hosts the quiz in which contestants answer questions to win turns on an arcade-style machine. Dropping tokens down a choice of four chutes, they hope to knock piles of them off a moving shelf - and the more they collect, the greater the prize fund. The player who has won the least amount is then eliminated, and the last one standing competes for a £10,000 jackpot

Supported on the wings by her friends, family and a few famous faces, can Zoe choose the right boxes and resist the Banker's tempting cash offers until just the right moment, in order to take home a fortune for her chosen charity?

A family team from Lincolnshire answer questions about top 10 lists from the realms of pop culture and general knowledge, and then try to score a perfect 10 in the final round to take home the prize money. Have they got what it takes to win a huge cash prize of £125,000?

Bradley Walsh presents as Raj Bisram, Danielle Harold, John Conteh and Roger Black pit their wits against one of the ruthless Chasers in the hope of winning a potential prize pot worth thousands of pounds. They must work as a team and play strategically to answer general knowledge questions against the clock and race down the game board to the exit without being caught

Ranvir Singh returns with the quiz, with Davina and Stephen, Catherine and Lisa, and Ben and Max taking on Riddlemaster Henry Lewis as they attempt to answer general knowledge questions and confusing conundrums. Only one team will make it through to the high-stakes final with a chance to win a cash prize

The last remaining duo have the opportunity to potentially double the money they won earlier or leave with nothing. Crossing words with the reigning champions this time are sisters Carol and Joanie and couple Alisa and Joe

p.t: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
p.d: Sue Barker discusses her life both on and off the tennis court, while actor Adrian Lukis talks about returning to his Mr Wickham roots. Plus, the programme joins the royal family at the Braemar Gathering, and celebrates the very best in autumnal wines in today's Best of British

Gaby Roslin and vet Bolu Eso meet a family who share their home with 37 animals, while they get up close with tarantulas and reveal how to help protect wildlife from pets. Plus, they see how therapy dog Chester brings comfort and joy to care home residents, meet guinea pigs and discover more about the fascinating behaviour of the animals people love

p.t: Gary Barlow's Food and Wine Tour: New Zealand
p.d: Gary and Jason Manford leave the camper van behind and board the Coastal Pacific train for one of New Zealand's great railway journeys. They take in epic views of the Pacific, keeping an eye out for penguins and dolphins, before arriving in Blenheim, in the heart of Marlborough wine country, where they ride through the vineyards on a tandem. After a day of coastlines, fine wines and questionable teamwork, Gary and Jason climb back into the camper van and continue their road trip through Marlborough

Alan Titchmarsh and the team create a cleverly designed family garden that's full of fun for pre-school tots without being a primary-coloured plastic eyesore for the grownups who share it. Alan, David Domoney, Katie Rushworth and Frances Tophill also give tips on creating a mini-maze, creative sandpits and how to use plants to give an adventurous exotic flavour to play areas
Round-up of the latest headlines

Scientist Dr Ian Malcolm reluctantly joins a research team on the island where his employer first designed genetically engineered dinosaurs. Meanwhile, a big-game hunter takes the chance to bag the biggest prize of all - a Tyrannosaurus rex. Steven Spielberg's dinosaur adventure sequel, starring Jeff Goldblum, Julianne Moore, Pete Postlethwaite and Richard Attenborough

While on leave to attend the wedding of his friend, CIA agent Felix Leiter, James Bond is asked to help with a secret mission to capture notorious drug baron, Franz Sanchez. Though successful, Sanchez later escapes and seeks revenge on Leiter, killing his new bride and leaving Leiter for dead. Incensed by this, Bond refuses his next mission from MI6 to go in search of Sanchez, leaving M with no alternative but to revoke Bond's licence to kill. Now considered a rogue agent, Bond goes undercover to pose as an assassin for hire within Sanchez's drug empire, to bring him down from the inside. Spy thriller, starring Timothy Dalton, Robert Davi, Carey Lowell, Talisa Soto and Benicio Del Toro
Round-up of the latest headlines

As the competition passes the halfway point, Gary Lineker tests the mettle of the remaining celebrities in a spine-chilling individual challenge. With no one to rely on but themselves, those with the most backbone are rewarded. A mystery box returns and one team captain must decide whether to gamble for a potential advantage - but nothing is ever predictable. In the team challenge, romance is in the air - but the love is short-lived as a cruel rule change sparks tension.

p.t: Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?
p.d: Another line-up of contestants answer questions that could change their lives - with the four lifelines Ask the Audience, Phone a Friend, 50-50 and Ask the Host available to them if they get stuck. Jeremy Clarkson hosts

While investigating a murder, detectives Emma Crane and Tom Radley find evidence of serious misconduct within Wakestead police, uncovering a web of lies, institutional cover-ups and moral compromise. Crime drama adapted from the novel of the same name by Charlotte Langley, starring Michelle Keegan and Douglas Booth

With only eight places available on each team, the mentors must choose carefully as they search for the UK's most exciting singing talent, with the Rewind button giving them the chance to bring back an artist they regret letting go

Stephen Mulhern hosts the game show, with Denise Lewis, Deborah Meaden and Kevin Whately all trying to say what they see, as they guess well-known phrases for the chance to win a £50,000 jackpot for their chosen good causes

A gang of streetwise penguins decides to escape from New York's Central Park Zoo and return to a life in the wild, but when Marty the zebra and his friends follow suit, they end up stranded in Africa on a jungle island without a clue about how to fend for themselves. Animated comedy, with the voices of Ben Stiller, David Schwimmer, Chris Rock, Jada Pinkett Smith and Sacha Baron Cohen

p.t: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
p.d: The teenage wizard is alarmed to learn a dangerous fugitive sorcerer is searching for him. Meanwhile, a new teacher at Hogwarts helps the bespectacled youngster to protect himself from the school's soul-sucking security guards. The third in the fantasy adventure series, starring Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson, Rupert Grint, Gary Oldman, David Thewlis, Michael Gambon, Robbie Coltrane and Alan Rickman

p.t: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
p.d: Adolescent wizard Harry is unexpectedly chosen to represent Hogwarts School in a prestigious magical tournament, despite being legally too young to enter. Along with charming sixth-year student Cedric Diggory, Harry takes on the champions of two other magical academies visiting the school, facing deadly monsters in a series of death-defying challenges. Meanwhile, the followers of the dreaded Lord Voldemort plot to restore their master to the land of the living. Fourth instalment of the fantasy saga, starring Daniel Radcliffe, Robbie Coltrane, Ralph Fiennes, Michael Gambon, Rupert Grint, Emma Watson, Brendan Gleeson and Robert Pattinson

Housemates live under 24-hour surveillance as they attempt to avoid eviction from the Big Brother house with the most unpopular housemates facing a public vote
Kate Lawler and GK Barry host exclusive interviews with evicted housemates, celebrity fans and special guests.

Part one of two. Pop busies himself organising a christening while awaiting the birth of his first grandchild - and still finds time to cast a beady eye over the contents of an elderly widow's home. Whimsical rural drama, starring David Jason, Pam Ferris, Philip Franks and Catherine Zeta-Jones

Part two of two. Preparations get under way for the christening, while Primrose loses her heart to a very confused vicar. Pop gets a black eye, Edith Pilchester tackles a gang of roving Teddy boys and Mademoiselle Dupont begins to feel ill. Drama, starring David Jason, Pam Ferris and Catherine Zeta-Jones

Sybil's determination to pursue her political leanings lands her in great danger when a fight breaks out at an election results meeting. Matthew's tenderness in caring for the would-be suffragette is noticed by her sisters, but it is Mary who is stunned to receive a marriage proposal. Bates is cleared of suspicion over the stolen wine, but offers his resignation rather than name the culprit. Drama, starring Maggie Smith, Hugh Bonneville and Elizabeth McGovern

Cora makes a discovery that throws the inheritance issue into chaos, and Mary is prompted to keep Matthew waiting for an answer to his proposal. Robert arranges for Mrs Patmore to see an eye specialist, and O'Brien digs up more compromising information about Bates, but the Earl's response comes as a surprise. Thomas leaves the Abbey and Mary exacts vengeance on Edith for her treachery, while the household is rocked by a shocking announcement. Drama, starring Maggie Smith, Hugh Bonneville and Elizabeth McGovern

It is November 1916, and the family and servants are getting the house ready for a concert to raise funds to treat more casualties from the front. Bates returns from London with a proposal for Anna, while Isobel informs Robert and Cora that Matthew is engaged and wants to bring his fiancee to Downton. O'Brien plays a trick on new maid Ethel after taking an instant dislike to her. Costume drama, starring Maggie Smith, Hugh Bonneville and Elizabeth McGovern

Isobel suggests using Downton as a place of convalescence following a distressing incident at the village hospital. Shell-shocked new valet Lang arrives as William gets his call-up papers, and Carson strives to keep standards high, but suffers a panic attack in front of the family. Lady Rosamund is eager to unearth Lavinia and Carlisle's secret after overhearing them arguing, and romance blossoms for both Edith and Mary. Costume drama, starring Jim Carter, Samantha Bond and Cal Macaninch

The wounded officers arrive at Downton and Matthew suggests he bring General Sir Herbert Strutt to inspect the new convalescent home - but Branson decides to spoil the visit after failing his army medical. Meanwhile, William's return results in an awkward surprise for Daisy, and Violet and Rosamund discover Lavinia's past misdeeds. Costume drama, starring Dan Stevens, Allen Leech, Thomas Howes, Maggie Smith and Zoe Boyle

Joe becomes a crucial witness at a murder mystery event when its host suddenly turns up dead - as a fishing trip with Gennaro proves decisive in cracking the case. Meanwhile, Elena plots to keep Angelica in Italy

Joe and Lara suspect murder when a diver drowns on a routine dive, while Angelica is convinced that Daniele is dealing in drugs. To make matters worse, when she slaps a rude diner at the restaurant later on, Joe gets involved and a violent fight erupts. Crime drama, starring Warren Brown and Cristiana Dell'Anna

When the author of a book that sparked a nationwide treasure hunt is found dead, Barnaby and Winter must unravel the cryptic clues to find the killer among a group of dedicated seekers. Detective drama, starring Neil Dudgeon, Nick Hendrix and Fiona Dolman

The rural bliss of Ferne Basset is rudely shattered by the discovery of an elderly resident's body in the river. When Barnaby and Troy descend on the village to ferret out the culprit, they get caught up in simmering backstage rivalries at a local amateur dramatics group that Joyce has recently joined - and the situation grows more sinister when one of the actors is tricked into killing himself in the middle of a performance

The Cornish detective's silver wedding celebrations are interrupted by a fresh outbreak of crime on his patch. Five dead bodies have been found on board an abandoned lorry at the ferry terminal and a fugitive is on the run. Jack Shepherd, Helen Masters and Jimmy Yuill star

Monica attempts to put her family's safety first, but she races into action when the killer's identity is discovered and she has the opportunity to save his final victim. Meanwhile, Nichol tries to get his mother to finally leave her husband and consider a future without him

Action from the latest matches, including Millwall v West Ham United at the Den, Wrexham v Southampton at the Raceourse Ground and Lincoln City v Swansea City at ProAmpac Stadium in the Championship
Brian Moore presents action from September 1980, including Tottenham Hotspur v Manchester United, Southampton v Brighton & Hove Albion and Manchester City v Arsenal
Richard Henwood takes a look back at the glory days of British wrestling, with some classic action from the archives

Gabbie Partington presents coverage of the quarter-finals from AFAS Live in Amsterdam, played over the best of 19 legs. Eventual champion Michael van Gerwen produced a fine display at this stage last year to overcome Luke Humphries 10-5. With analysis from Glen Durrant and Chris Mason

Ali Hamidi is joined by Bobby Zamora and diver Luc Boerrigter as they return to The Lake of Dreams, aka Grenville. Having failed to land one of the lake's giants in front of the underwater cameras on their previous trip here together, this time they target a huge carp of over 60lbs. Being spring, the carp are constantly on the move around the lake, with the team in hot pursuit. Will the carp run rings around the team, or will the mobile tactics pay off to bank that big one?
Discover how crystal glasses are hand-blown from globs of red-hot molten glass. Plus, a look at how some of the finest single malt whisky in the world is produced

Gabby Partington presents coverage of the semi-finals and final from AFAS Live in Amsterdam. Michael van Gerwen was the victorious player in 2025, defeating Josh Rock 11-6 in the last four, before ending the reign of 2024 champion Luke Littler with an 11-7 triumph in the showpiece match to win this title for a record-extending sixth occasion. However, having enjoyed an outstanding year so far, Littler will have gone into the tournament expecting to regain the title, and it would be a surprise if he had not reached the semi-finals. With analysis from Glen Durrant and Chris Mason

An Arizona sheriff is sent to New York to bring an imprisoned murderer back to stand trial. However, when the killer escapes, the lawman employs his own methods to recapture him, antagonising the city's by-the-book police force in the process. Don Siegel's crime drama, starring Clint Eastwood, Lee J Cobb, Don Stroud and Susan Clark

Neville is suspended for lying about being a joiner, but manages to redeem himself by averting a disaster on the site. He is not only reinstated by Herr Ulrich, but allowed to work as a bricklayer - which is bad news for Oz, who is sacked to make way for him. Drama, starring Tim Healy, Kevin Whately, Timothy Spall and Jimmy Nail

When Hannibal auditions for a children's show, the team is bemused - until discovering it is a front for a drug ring. Action adventure, starring Mr T and George Peppard
Murdock is abducted after winning a Hawaiian holiday. Action adventure, starring Dwight Schultz and George Peppard
The team tries to prevent an insane Soviet general starting World War Three. Action adventure, starring Mr T and George Peppard

A family in Los Angeles finds itself separated during a convergence of history's greatest disasters - a super volcano, a mega earthquake and a massive twister. Sci-fi drama, starring Matthew Pohlkamp, Natalie Pelletier and Erich Riegelmann

A disastrous energy experiment unleashes a series of devastating hurricanes across America. A science teacher realises the movement of the winds into each other will result in a single continent-destroying storm, and tries to get his family to safety before it is too late. Adventure, starring Casper Van Dien and Michael Beach

The Earth faces destruction from a black hole in space causing environmental disasters across the world. As a fleet of space arks is constructed to save the human race, a team of scientists ventures into the South American jungle in search of 12 magical skulls that can save the world from destruction. Fantasy adventure, starring Richard Burgi and Wendy Glenn

A charming bank robber breaks out of jail and takes a female US Marshal hostage. Managing to escape, she sets out to track him down as he prepares for one last job - but as the chase intensifies, so do their feelings for each other. Steven Soderbergh's romantic crime drama, based on Elmore Leonard's novel, with George Clooney, Jennifer Lopez, Ving Rhames and Don Cheadle

A hitman is targeted by fellow assassins after a crisis of conscience leaves him unwilling to complete his latest contract. While trying to escape with his life, he encounters a female forger, and the duo embark on an explosive rampage as they battle to survive. Action thriller, starring Chow Yun-Fat, Mira Sorvino, Michael Rooker and Kenneth Tsang

A timid, downtrodden housewife gets drawn into a confrontation with a street gang, who later drive her car off the road. She flees into the forest with the thugs in hot pursuit, and uses the contents of her toolbox to fight for her life. Thriller, starring Kim Basinger, Lukas Haas and Craig Sheffer.

Invaders from outer space take over a remote Scottish island and raise the temperature to an unbearable level, giving residents little or no chance of survival. Sci-fi adventure, starring Christopher Lee, Peter Cushing and Patrick Allen
As Earth prepares to close down the station, Bester tries to persuade Sheridan to return to the Shadow homeworld
A news reporter visits the station, there is bad news for Sheridan, and Dr Franklin battles to save the telepaths. Sci-fi adventure, starring Bruce Boxleitner
A man recruits a prospector to help him save his sister, but is forced to endure a terrible challenge to bring her safely home. Western, starring Richard Boone and Stewart Petersen

The desperate relatives of people captured by Comanches many years before put pressure on the US military to bring them home. The army hires a cynical frontier marshal, who agrees to negotiate their release in return for a commission. But the townsfolk are forced to face some grim truths when he returns with just one unrecognisable captive. John Ford's Western, with James Stewart, Richard Widmark and Shirley Jones

A greedy and corrupt businessman rules over a prospecting town, claiming ownership over the gold-rich land and using violence to keep the locals in line. Help comes from an unlikely source when two gunslingers join forces with a travelling circus to free the townsfolk from his control. Comedy Western, starring Terence Hill and Bud Spencer, with Woody Strode and Victor Buono

Two hot-headed brothers set off to find the wreckage of an aircraft in the Alps - one intending to loot it, the other determined to stop him. But when they finally reach their goal, there's a surprise in store that forces the feuding siblings to deal with their differences once and for all. Drama, starring Spencer Tracy and Robert Wagner

A girl strikes a deadly bargain with a witch in order to catch the eye of the man she desires

Unconventional submarine skipper Joe Glass is sent to investigate the torpedoing of US and Russian vessels. He winds up trying to rescue the Russian president, who has been kidnapped by a rogue general. Action thriller, starring Gerard Butler, Gary Oldman and Common

An American takes a job in an Asian nation and relocates his family overseas. However, no sooner do they arrive then a revolution takes the country by storm. They face a struggle for survival as the new government seeks to eliminate all foreigners. Action thriller, starring Owen Wilson, Pierce Brosnan and Lake Bell

A British military contractor leaves Afghanistan for Los Angeles when he receives word that his daughter has died there. However, he discovers the body identified as her is someone else, and embarks on a rampage of violence through the criminal underworld to discover what has really happened to her. Action thriller, starring Craig Fairbrass, Jason Patric and James Caan
Former outlaw Nathaniel Reed's peaceful existence on the Texas frontier is shattered when a vengeful US Marshal starts hunting him down. Western, starring Trace Adkins
Buying goods from the comfort of home
A karate student joins a gang to avenge those responsible for shooting his brother, and Walker attempts to restore order to the neighbourhood before Christmas

Danni Menzies helps Lincolnshire farmers David and Debbie, who are looking for a holiday home, in and around the town of Coin in Spain's Málaga Province. The pair want a place that's big enough to house their five children and Woody, their horse, within a budget of £230,000
Laura Hamilton helps motorbike enthusiast Jennie look for a home on the western Costa del Sol. With a budget of £85,000, Laura lines up five impressive properties

Sara Damergi heads to Poitou-Charentes in the west of France to help house-hunters Jules and Gaynor. Along with their pet alpacas, they're planning a permanent move to rural France to run their own gîte business. Sara shows them the best of what their £250,000 budget can buy in the local market
Craig Rowe helps photographer and videographer Geoff to find a holiday home on the Caribbean island of Barbados, with Geoff's friend Alan on board to size up potential properties

Ben Hillman heads to the inland towns and villages of Almería province in southern Spain to help house-hunters Candy and Mark find the perfect holiday home. The couple, who are planning to get married in six months' time, are looking for a rural retreat to escape to whenever they can. Ben shows them five attractive options for their budget of £75,000

Semi-retired children's nurse Tracey is looking for a holiday home in La Duquesa on Spain's Costa del Sol and she brings along her friend Jackie for moral support. Property expert Jasmine Harman has five attempts to find Tracey the perfect place on a budget of £140,000

Peppa and Rebecca Rabbit pretend to be babies to get Mummy Rabbit's attention. Mummy Rabbit plays along until they admit they are not really babies!

Rome created the largest empire in the ancient world - its armies, organisation and building innovation created a vast territory linked by roads. Many of these cities lie in ruins today, others are buried and many others are forgotten. As this documentary reveals, they include Leptis Magna, Volubilis, Tipasa and Timgad in North Africa and Baalbek, Jerash, Palmyra and Apamea in the Middle East

Exploring five examples of harmless symbols that have been turned into dangerous propaganda tools for movements that have hunted, tortured and killed, including the Hitler salute, the swastika, the Z of the Russian war against Ukraine, the Q of QAnon and the Star of David

With access to the first nationwide survey and state-of-the-art drones mapping the Great Wall of China, this documentary offers new evidence that reveals its extraordinary magnitude, rewrites its millennia-long history and decodes its complex signals system. Using cutting-edge chemistry, the programme also finds out what has kept the wall standing for so long - a simple cooking ingredient found in kitchens across the world

p.t: Grand Tours of the Scottish Islands
p.d: Paul Murton explores the Isle of Mull and its satellite islands to discover why they have become boltholes from the hustle and bustle of the modern world. He begins on the tidal island of Erraid, which inspired famous Scottish writer Robert Louis Stevenson, then hops over to Ulva, the final resting place of Lachlan MacQuarrie, one of the first governors of New South Wales. He then explores Mull itself, being given a whistlestop tour of the island by rally driver Louise Thomas, then travels to the mysterious little island of Inch Kenneth, where he hears the story of Nazi sympathizer Unity Mitford. He ends his tour at the remote Treshnish Islands, where he experiences a spot of 'puffin therapy'

In the 1950s, Havana shines as a vibrant metropolis - alive with music, casinos, and cabarets. However, beneath the allure lies a city controlled by the American mafia, where luxury contrasts sharply with the poverty endured by most Cubans. American tourists escape Prohibition and moral restrictions back home. Many schoolboys get together to form a band, but few of them go on to become multi-million-selling recording artists - but that's what happened to Genesis. Its core members - Peter Gabriel, Mike Rutherford and Tony Banks - met at Charterhouse, a public school in Surrey, and began playing together with two other students in 1967. A few years and personnel changes later (including the addition of drummer Phil Collins) and the classic line-up was in place. But relationships within the band were fraught; Gabriel left for a solo career in 1975, and Rutherford, Collins, Banks and Steve Hackett carried on without him. Here, they're back together again to discuss their careers. Rare archive footage helps tell the story

A special tribute concert for the late George Harrison, filmed at the Royal Albert Hall, and featuring surviving Beatles Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr performing together for the first time since 1969. Eric Clapton, Jeff Lynne, Tom Petty, Ravi Shankar, Jools Holland and George's son Dhani sing renditions of classic hits including Something, Taxman, My Sweet Lord and My Guitar Gently Weeps. The members of Monty Python, whose film Life of Brian was bankrolled by Harrison, are also reunited for the event to perform a selection of their own comic songs with the aid of Hollywood megastar Tom Hanks

p.t: The Rolling Stones: Welcome to Shepherd's Bush
p.d: A 1999 concert by the band at Shepherd's Bush Empire, featuring performances of Honky Tonk Women, Route 66, Tumbling Dice, Brown Sugar and Jumpin' Jack Flash

Alan Yentob visits France to introduce a film documenting the recording of the Rolling Stones' 1972 album Exile on Main Street. Having faced ruin due to the size of their unpaid tax bills, the Stones relocated to the French Riviera to make the album, before completing the recording in Los Angeles - with Mick Jagger also finding time to get married in St Tropez. Alongside rare home-movie footage of the band at work, there are also interviews with Jagger, Keith Richards, Bill Wyman and Charlie Watts
The singer's concert at the Blockbuster Pavilion in San Bernardino, California, which was part of her What's Love tour in 1993
With a helping hand from the likes of Mavis Staples, Janis Joplin and Chaka Khan, this documentary takes a trip to the 1950s and 60s to the roots of rock 'n' roll
The story behind the Sex Pistols' sole studio album, 1977's Never Mind the B*******, Here's the Sex Pistols. Featuring interviews with singer John Lydon and manager Malcolm McLaren

From London's Royal Albert Hall, Pete Townshend, the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, conductor Robert Ziegler and a host of guests, including Alfie Boe, put a classical spin on the Who's 1973 album Quadrophenia
Bob Ross uses a golden selection of colours in this mountain scene, all inside a unique oval shape on canvas
Bobby sets his sights on buying an NFL franchise, while Lara launches her own business venture. Chuck makes a last ditch effort to nail a big case

Under pressure to make progress and with his case stalling, Chuck develops a new strategy. Axe considers donating half his net worth to charity. Wendy helps a tech billionaire assess a candidate for a special project. Drama, starring Paul Giamatti and Damian Lewis
Part one of two. Falsone and Stivers take a case involving bounty hunters who killed the wrong man while in pursuit of a fugitive. Police drama, starring Toni Lewis and Jon Seda

Part two of two. Gharty's impending meeting with the divorce lawyers leaves him feeling fraught, Lewis is rushed to hospital after McGee's accident and Gee refuses to cooperate with the bounty hunters. Peter Gerety and Yaphet Kotto star

Part one of two. Kellerman defends a girl accused of murder after a newborn baby's body is found buried behind a hotel _ and advises his client that she should try to implicate her boyfriend. Reed Diamond stars
Part two of two. Debbie signs the plea agreement implicating Craig in the murder of the baby, but Falsone wants more time to work on the case
A riot is sparked when a bus strikes a black female pedestrian. The white driver is killed in the uproar and, some distance away, another body is found
As George fights to protect his public image, Agnes' status quo is disrupted and Armstrong intensifies her campaign against Peggy
As Edison's illuminating electricity demonstration sparks conversation, George prepares for a legal battle and Bannister plots revenge
Bertha is reminded of her place on her visit to Newport, George gets his day in court, Peggy reveals the truth about her past and Gladys and Carrie practise for the ball
As Ada and Aurora rush to stop Marian from making a huge decision, Bertha and Mrs Astor's clash impacts all of New York society
It is Easter morning 1883 and Bertha Russell receives news that her bid for a box at the Academy of Music has been rejected. The return of the period drama, starring Carrie Coon and Louisa Jacobson

Crozier demands that Franklin send out a sledge party to seek help, but he is reluctant to risk any more of his men. The resulting clash leads Franklin to condemn Crozier for his alcoholism, prompting his devastated old friend to take matters into his own hands, drafting a resignation letter and taking personal responsibility for finding help

A cunning attack on the ships proves the men are not battling an ordinary bear and that the region's Inuit culture may hold a key to their survival. Back in England, Franklin's wife and niece put pressure on the Admiralty to organise a rescue mission - and when they are refused, they decide to fund one themselves
As four misfit kids vow to find their missing classmate, Major Leroy Hanlon arrives at Derry Air Force Base
